students' intention to emigrate is a complex phenomenon, influenced by a number of individual, social and economic factors, and that it is not possible to identify a single factor that can predict the intention to emigrate.

medical students from Serbia, especially those from the fifth year, have a higher probability of migrating to work abroad and that this probability is higher among students from Belgrade, students with a higher family income, students who intend to work abroad and students who do not have plans to work in Serbia.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
medical students in Serbia have high intentions to work abroad.
the majority of students in Serbia are not planning to work abroad, however those who do intend to work abroad have a strong desire to do so.

medical students' intention and plans to work abroad are related with the desire to improve their knowledge and experience, the lack of opportunities for further education and employment in Serbia, and the desire to work and earn abroad.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of students are not intending to leave Serbia, however, a substantial number of students have plans to work in other countries.
medical students' intention to migrate abroad is a complex issue that requires a comprehensive approach to address the problem.
